name: Robin's Egg Blue
lede: Robin's Egg Blue is a paler, lighter variant of Robin's Egg, recorded by Maerz and Paul in 1930 and found exactly once in our painting archive.

sections.title: The paler half of a pair
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary is cited by the NBS Circular of 1955 as the source for this hue, which the ISCC-NBS system itself files as block 149, a pale green [1]. The crowd-sourced xkcd color survey of 2010 also records a close match [1]. It is the paler, lighter sibling of [[robin-s-egg|Robin's Egg]], 4.0 units away by our measure, the two sharing the same bird-egg word but sitting at different lightness and chroma [2].

Past that sibling, the nearest neighbor is [[pale-turquoise|Pale Turquoise]], 4.4 units away; [[celeste|Celeste]] and [[pale-sky-blue|Pale Sky Blue]] are both about 5.1 units off [2]. In LCH terms Robin's Egg Blue measures lightness 90, chroma 27, hue 209 degrees, paler and less saturated than its namesake [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Robin's Egg Blue in exactly 1 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, rarer than 86 percent of the archive's named colors [3]. That single match is a 1904 work by Maurice Denis, where the color plays a hidden role rather than carrying the light [3]. A single match is too thin to support any claim about century, country or painter beyond this one painting, and the hex itself remains a screen approximation [3].
